Common questions

Let’s clear a few things up.

Useful answers before you build your first plan.

What does DegreeSteps help me do?

DegreeSteps helps you build a starting degree plan around your goals, preferred school, existing learning, and priorities. It brings outside-credit options, degree requirements, open questions, and next steps into one place.

Can I really take courses outside my university?

Many schools consider credit from other colleges, approved exams, military learning, and courses with ACE or NCCRS recommendations. Acceptance and degree placement depend on the exact school, program, course, dates, and your individual evaluation.

Does an ACE recommendation guarantee transfer credit?

No. ACE makes credit recommendations; it does not accredit a provider as a college or require schools to accept a course. The receiving school decides whether the learning is accepted and which degree requirements it satisfies.

Can this work for an on-campus degree?

It can. A residential program may allow outside learning before enrollment or while enrolled, subject to its own policies. Campus attendance, major requirements, institutional-credit minimums, and course availability still need to be planned.

Do I need transcripts to get started?

No. You can build a clearly provisional starting plan and add original learning records later. DegreeSteps never guesses earned credits from a rough estimate. An official evaluation is needed to establish your individual awards.

Can DegreeSteps tell me the cheapest or fastest degree?

Your priority shapes the suggested path. A reliable final price and finish date also require current school fees, approved credits, your pace, prerequisites, and actual course schedules. Missing information remains visible rather than being treated as zero cost or instant completion.

Which degrees can I build a plan for?

The degree picker shows available course-by-course templates. You can also build a private plan or research a degree from its official link. School-resource pages cover a wider selection of colleges; those overviews do not imply that every program has a complete transfer plan.

How do community-verified transfers work?

Student reports add real-world evidence for a particular placement and catalog. Verification uses evidence rules rather than popularity alone. Community feedback helps identify a promising match or a problem; it cannot establish your own school-approved credit award.

Is DegreeSteps free?

Yes. DegreeSteps is free to use: exploring plans, building your plan and saving it to your free account cost nothing. Courses, tuition and provider fees are separate. See why DegreeSteps is free

Will a degree path qualify me for a licensed profession?

Teaching, law, aviation, and health professions can require approved preparation, clinical or classroom work, examinations, and jurisdiction-specific licensing. DegreeSteps keeps those checks separate from simply completing academic credits.
